_comment: Repo allowlist for scripts/hermes-cc.sh. ABSENCE IS A DENIAL — hermes-cc.sh accepts a
repo NAME from this file and resolves the path itself, so the agent never names a
filesystem path and cannot reach a repo that is not listed here.
maxTier caps what a dispatch into that repo may do, independently of what the caller
asks for. A repo's tier is the CEILING, not the default — every dispatch still defaults
to 'investigate' unless it asks for more, and 'implement' additionally needs --why and
--confirm no matter how high the ceiling is.
investigate  read-only. Cannot lose anything.
author       + files one GitHub issue. A wrong issue is closed in two seconds.
implement    + an isolated worktree, a dispatch/… branch and a DRAFT pull request.
Never a merge, never a push to a default branch, never a CI workflow.
HOW THE CEILINGS BELOW WERE CHOSEN. The question is not 'could an episode damage this
repo' — it cannot, since nothing merges — but 'is an unreviewed draft PR here useful or
just noise', and 'what does this repo control if a bad change ever did land'.
implement  Repos where the bridge itself lives (hermes-agent, sideclaw) — closing its
own loop is the actual use case — plus small self-contained tools where a
draft PR is cheap to read. And dispatch-scratch, which exists only to be
dispatched into.
author     Application and service repos. Triage that finds a real defect should be
able to record it; proposing the code change unattended is not yet earned.
investigate  dotfiles, vps, homelab. These are the machine's own control plane:
dotfiles carries the secrets tooling and the rules that bound every agent
on this box (including this one), and vps/homelab are deployment surfaces
watched by rollhook. Read-only here is a deliberate floor, not an oversight.
DELIBERATELY ABSENT, and staying absent:
dotfiles-private, homelab-private — private by construction. Their whole point is
that their contents are not referenced from anywhere else; an agent-readable
episode inside them would undo that.
brain — the personal vault. Read-only would be technically safe, but journal and
personal notes are not triage material, and the obsidian skill already owns that
door with conventions this tool does not implement.
